messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: new argument refactor: doc on adapt-engaged?
parts:
May I ask what will happen if I set engaged to 0?  I did not find the doc about it. 

And I did not find the doc about arguments gamma, delta, kappa.  If I did not miss the doc somewhere, I think they need to be doced or pointed to a reference. 

--
Jiqiang

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] new argument refactor: doc on adapt-engaged?
parts:
It's documented in both the LaTeX and the help output,

adapt
Warmup Adaptation
Valid subarguments: engaged, gamma, delta, kappa, t0

engaged=<boolean>
Adaptation engaged?
Valid values: [0, 1]
Defaults to 1

gamma=<double>
Adaptation regularization scale
Valid values: 0 < gamma
Defaults to 0.05

delta=<double>
Adaptation target acceptance statistic
Valid values: 0 < delta < 1
Defaults to 0.65

kappa=<double>
Adaptation relaxation exponent
Valid values: 0 < kappa
Defaults to 0.75

t0=<double>
Adaptation iteration offset
Valid values: 0 < t0
Defaults to 10

engaged=0 turns off adaptation (engaged=false without quotes might also work, depending on how the local system interprets booleans).

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] new argument refactor: doc on adapt-engaged?
parts:
Oh, I see what you mean.

Warmup and adaptation are two different things. A warmup period allows the Markov chain to converge to the target distribution -- this is always required of an MCMC method. In Stan we also take advantage of the warmup period to perform various adaptation routines -- these are not necessary but can be helpful for performance. Turning adaptation off leaves all algorithmic parameters at their nominal values and just tries to converge to the target distribution.
